We are hiring for this position in Trinity’s Waltham, MA office or NYC offices.

Trinity Life Sciences is looking for a talented, committed, and energetic individual to join our team as a Data Science Intern to support our growing Enterprise Analytics Delivery (EAD) function. - Assist senior staff and project managers to adhere to project timelines by providing ongoing support to client for existing engagements

- Develop an understanding of industry secondary data sources available and weigh pros and cons of leveraging each data source available

Education: Enrolled in a Bachelor’s (must be rising senior) or Master’s program in business, engineering, mathematics, biostatistics, data science, economics or life sciences disciplines at a top-tier university.

- Desire and ability to work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment

- Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint is required

- Have strong technical ability in data analysis of large datasets, particularly with healthcare data

- Self-motivated, willing to take initiative, and appropriately independent

- Enthusiasm for working collaboratively in a team-based environment

- Strong problem solving and logical thinking skill

- Excellent communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills

- Familiarity with healthcare terms (e.g., ICD, HCPCS/CPT, NDC) is a nice to have

SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world.

Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in.

Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience: Built for early career talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you’re in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. You’ll dive into meaningful projects and tasks that sharpen your skills and deepen your knowledge. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Your time with us will culminate in an opportunity to showcase your contributions and learnings to SharkNinja leaders because this is a program for those ready to shape what’s next — fast.

Do you notice the ad before you notice the product? Do you want to know why one video gets three million views and the next one gets three thousand? Are you excited by the challenge of building demand for products that end up in millions of homes? If so, we invite you to learn more about Marketing, Creative & eCommerce Co-op opportunities at SharkNinja.

This is a single application for marketing, creative, communications, and eCommerce early talent roles across SharkNinja. The hiring teams are spread across our brand marketing, integrated communications, social and content, creative and studio, and eCommerce and marketplace functions.

Whichever team you join, you’ll work on real campaigns and real launches alongside people who have run them before. You might be cutting a short-form video the week a product drops, answering consumers in the brand voice, building the retailer page that converts them, pricing against a competitor on a marketplace, or writing the copy that goes on the box. If you’re curious, consumer-obsessed, fast-moving, and ready to make an impact from day one, we want to hear from you!

- Integrated Marketing Communications

- Corporate Communications

- Copywriting

- LATAM Marketing

- Paid & Performance Media

- Social (Shark and LATAM)

- Global Social Operations

- Creative Operations

- Build assets people actually see — social content, campaign creative, packaging copy, retailer pages, email, and video

Brand, Integrated Marketing & Communications

Role Summary

As a Software Engineering Intern, you will support the Infotainment Platform Enablement team focused on next-generation infotainment platforms. The team enables early hardware bring-up develops manufacturing validation software, and builds system-level workload emulation and diagnostics frameworks to de-risk high compute automotive platforms well ahead of production. This role offers hands-on exposure to embedded systems, hardware-software integration, vehicle workload emulation, and large-scale diagnostics telemetry systems running on cutting-edge compute platforms.

Responsibilities

- Contribute to the design and implementation of a Software Application Framework for infotainment and validation systems

- Support hardware bring-up and validation of Electrical Control Units (ECUs)

- Develop test utilities and manufacturing software in C/C++ and Python

- Assist in emulating vehicle workloads to validate system behavior and power/performance characteristics

- Debug hardware and software integration issues across subsystems (camera, display, audio, connectivity, sensors)

- Collect, analyze, and visualize diagnostics telemetry data to support root cause analysis

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver scalable solutions

About the Team

DoorDash Labs is DoorDash's autonomous delivery group, building the robots and hardware that move goods without a driver. The Vehicle Electrical team designs the electronics at the core of these systems, including power and motor-control electronics, charging, and the test benches that prove the whole system works.

About the Role

As a summer intern, you will own a defined hardware project in one of three areas: an on-board charger prototype, an in-house motor control circuit, or a full-power hardware test bench with motor power and battery simulation. You will take it from requirements through design, build, and bench validation, and present your results to the team at the end of the summer. You will report into the Director, Electrical Engineering in our DoorDash Labs organization.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

- Own an end-to-end project in one of three areas: an on-board charger prototype, an in-house motor control circuit, or a full-power hardware test bench.

- Design, build, and bring up hardware, from schematic and component selection through prototype assembly and debug.

- Characterize your design on the bench with lab equipment, measuring efficiency, thermal, and control performance against requirements.

- Collaborate with power electronics, firmware, and test engineers, and incorporate design review feedback into your work.

- Document your results and present your findings to the team at the end of your internship.

We're excited about you because…

- You are pursuing a B.S. or M.S. Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent, have no more than 2 years of full-time work experience, and are graduating between Fall 2027 to Summer 2028.

- You are available for a May or June 2027 start date (Internships are only hosted during the Summer).

- You have coursework or project experience in power electronics, including switch-mode converters (buck, boost, PFC, isolated DC-DC), gate drive, magnetics, and power-stage design.

- You understand motor control fundamentals, including BLDC/PMSM drives, inverter half-bridges, field-oriented control, and current and position sensing.

- You understand analog and feedback-control fundamentals, including op-amp sensing circuits, ADC signal conditioning, loop compensation, and stability analysis.

- You can capture schematics and lay out PCBs in a tool such as Altium or KiCad, with awareness of high-current layout, thermal, and EMC considerations.

- You understand lithium-ion battery charging (CC/CV profiles, protection limits) and how a battery management system interfaces with a charger or load.

- You have hands-on lab experience with oscilloscopes, differential probes, power supplies, and electronic loads, and can safely debug high-current, high-voltage hardware.

- You can write Python or C/C++ for instrument automation, data acquisition, or microcontroller bring-up.

- You are able to work onsite at our Oakland, CA office.

Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis

Master Data Management Intern

Department: Data Management / Transformation Office

Job Summary

A Master Data Management (MDM) intern assists with organizing, cleaning, and governing core enterprise data assets like product, customer, or supplier information across systems.

Essential Duties

We are seeking a motivated, detail-oriented, and analytical Master Data Management (MDM) Intern to join our data team. In this role, you will gain hands-on experience supporting enterprise-wide data governance, data quality, and system integration initiatives. You will work closely with data stewards, IT professionals, and business stakeholders to help maintain a reliable, accurate "single source of truth" for critical business data.

- Data Cleansing & Validation: Assist in data collection, auditing, profiling, and cleansing activities to identify anomalies and ensure high data quality across enterprise platforms.
- Process & Governance Documentation: Help document data flows, standard operating procedures (SOPs), data dictionaries, and governance policies.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with business units and technical teams to research data discrepancies, answer inquiries, and support root-cause analysis for data issues.
- Project Support: Participate in active MDM system migrations, software upgrades, or testing initiatives (such as validating data models, user acceptance testing, or report building).

About the Team

The DoorDash Research Fellowship is a 3-month program (extendable to 6 months) looking for Summer and Fall 2026 cohorts, for researchers and engineers who want to work on the hardest applied ML and AI problems in local commerce. Fellows are given the resources, autonomy, and access to real-world operational data needed to pursue ambitious research directions — with the goal of producing work that influences both the field and how DoorDash operates at scale.

This program is modeled on the best external research fellowships: fellows are treated as independent researchers, not as junior employees on a product team. You pick the problem (within a set of priority areas), you own the direction, and you publish or ship the outcome.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will receive…

- Dedicated compute allocation sized to the research agenda — GPU clusters for training and inference budgets for experimentation

- Full access to DoorDash's research infrastructure — our internal RL stack, training and evaluation pipelines, RL environments built on real operational systems, agent evaluation harnesses, and the tooling our own research teams use day-to-day. Fellows are first-class users, not sandboxed visitors.

- Access to DoorDash operational data — real-world datasets spanning logistics, merchant operations, consumer behavior, and marketplace dynamics, under appropriate data governance

- Research mentorship from senior researchers and engineering leaders at DoorDash, plus a named research sponsor for each fellow who meets with you weekly and is accountable for unblocking your work

- Speaker series featuring leading researchers and practitioners from academia and industry — faculty from top ML programs, research leads from frontier AI labs, and senior operators from across tech. Fellows get dedicated 1:1 time with speakers when possible.

- A cohort of fellows working alongside you — a small, tight-knit group of researchers tackling different problems but sharing ideas, drafts, and reading groups. The community extends to DoorDash research alumni and the broader fellowship network.

- Publication support — fellows are encouraged to publish at top venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, KDD, etc.) and DoorDash will support the legal and review process

- Relocation support, housing stipend, and competitive pay

Structure

- Kickoff (2 weeks, in-person in SF): Onboarding, scoping the research agenda with your sponsor, meeting teams across Research, ML Platform, and relevant product orgs

- Core research period (~10 weeks, hybrid from SF DoorDash office): Focused research work with regular check-ins, internal talks, and working sessions. Extension to 6 months decided at the midpoint based on research progress and mutual fit.

- Closeout: Final write-up, internal presentation, and publication or productionization path

Priority Research Areas

Fellows are welcome to propose their own direction, but we are particularly interested in work across:

- Reinforcement learning environments for real-world operations — building high-fidelity simulators and training environments from operational data, including the tradeoffs between real-data fidelity and synthetic generalization

- Agentic systems for logistics and local commerce — long-horizon planning, tool use, and evaluation methodologies for agents operating in physical-world marketplaces

- Foundation models for marketplace dynamics — forecasting, pricing, matching, and personalization at marketplace scale

- Evaluation and measurement — new benchmarks and evaluation methods for ML systems deployed in messy, real-world operational settings

- Multimodal understanding — vision, speech, and language applied to merchant catalogs, operations, and consumer interfaces

We’re excited about you because…

- You’re a researcher with a strong track record — PhD candidates (rising 4th year or beyond), recent PhDs, or independent researchers with published work at top ML venues or equivalent demonstrated output

- You’re an engineer with deep research instincts who have shipped ambitious ML or systems work and want dedicated time to pursue a research direction

- You can operate independently — set a research agenda, scope it, and execute without heavy supervision

- You have strong written and verbal communication; comfort presenting work to mixed research and engineering audiences

We are not looking for specific years of experience or specific degrees. Exceptional candidates from non-traditional backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.

Compensation

The fellowship is 12 weeks long with potential opportunity for extension. The fellow’s starting pay will fall within the monthly pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including education, work location, and market conditions.

Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base pay, fellows are eligible for both a housing stipend and relocation stipend. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer our fellows a wellness reimbursement benefit, access to an employee assistance program, in-office lunch credits and more!

Base Pay (Monthly)

$8,500—$16,000 USD

We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

What to Expect

Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to de-bottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.

Job Overview

You will build and operate the test infrastructure we use to validate grid-tied converters. This role owns a meaningful slice of the development loop: test bench design and build, test execution, data analysis, failure isolation, and verified fixes. You will uncover real design and process failures by running physical tests and building automated equipment and data workflows. We prioritize a strong foundation in first principles, practical skill, and a bias toward getting things done. We care as much about how you work as what you already know.

How You Will Contribute

Test Bench Architecture & Build

- Design and build electrical reliability test benches for power electronics hardware—inverters, DC/DC converters, bi-directional power stages.

- Specify, procure, and integrate lab equipment: programmable power supplies, electronic loads, DAQ systems, sensors, protection hardware, interlocks, and cabling.

- Own the bench system design: grounding, measurement integrity, EMI-aware instrumentation, protection strategy, safe operating procedures, and maintainability.

Software & Test Automation

- Contribute to our software test infrastructure for system integration and reliability testing — test architecture, hardware abstraction layers, and result reporting pipelines.

- Write software tests that interact directly with hardware and firmware over CAN, UART, Modbus, TCP/IP — debugging signal integrity, protocol failures, and firmware edge cases.

- Write concurrent, fault-tolerant software for our next-generation manufacturing test platform: Firmware Flashing, FCT, EOL stations running autonomously on the factory floor.

- Build AI agents that manage test execution across facilities — initiating runs, monitoring anomalies, implementing test script and firmware changes in response to failures, and routing issues to humans

Test Execution & Reliability Campaigns

- Translate test goals and suspected failure mechanisms into test plans, stress profiles, instrumentation plans, and pass/fail criteria.

- Execute reliability campaigns—burn-in, power cycling, thermal stress, and abuse tests—and evolve them as we learn where the real failure cliffs are.

- Drive fast debug loops during excursions: isolate, instrument deeper, reproduce, and verify that corrective actions eliminate the failure.

What You Will Bring

We prioritize a strong foundation in first principles, practical skill, an inquisitive mindset, and a proactive attitude. We care as much—or more—about how you work as what you already know.

Must-Have Requirements

- Pursuing a BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field.

- Hands-on experience designing, building, or operating electrical test setups for complex hardware—power electronics strongly preferred.

- Comfort with bench power equipment and measurement methods: scopes, DMMs, power analyzers, electronic loads, DAQ, and sensors.

- Ability to design safe test systems for high-power hardware: interlocks, protection, grounding, and safe operating procedures.

- Strong debugging instincts and ability to drive root-cause closure with engineering partners.

- Programming experience in Python—including instrument control or data automation.

Nice-to-Haves

- Experience with accelerated or environmental stress testing (HALT/HASS, thermal/humidity cycling, power cycling).

- Familiarity with failure mechanisms in power electronics and structured root cause/corrective action loops.

- Experience designing repeatable test cells with drawings and instructions to turn scrappy setups into production-quality ones.

If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power.
